card.serve_args_note: fixed state backing: hrx-loom 0.2.0's default elastic backing costs Strix 5-8 % steady prefill and a 3-request ramp (small models most); fixed backing commits the preset's context_capacity KV and the weights eagerly, and the packages already cap context_capacity to what fits the Strix budget
card.preload_note: preload: --parameter_mode=preload (stock-host fix for ROCm/hrx-system#3332: the default parameter mode fails under the stock 8 MiB RLIMIT_MEMLOCK on Linux 7.0) is served only where the preloaded host copy fits beside GPU memory in the shared RAM: packages whose weights are at most this many bytes (decimal; the 35B-A3B class passed, the 122B OOMs); larger packages keep the default parameter mode and the card's Quick start says how to start on a stock host

strix-halo.name: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 "Strix Halo" (gfx1151)
strix-halo.note: LPDDR5X-8000, 256-bit (256 GB/s peak); bw MEASURED: 228 GB/s, Loom streaming read of 1 GiB (+64 MiB written; copy of 512 MiB the same), loom-benchmark dispatch_complete, 8 launches per batch, on a DevLab Strix Halo runner with and without the active wait (completion_spin_ns), hrx-loom 0.2.0, run 44388427539 (the same kernel: 611 GB/s on the R9700S). The earlier 216 GB/s sat under it: Loom dense decode and 4-stream rows measured above their ceilings (e.g. Nanbeige4.3-33B decode 105 %, Gemma 4 31B 4 streams 104 %). flops: the spec-sheet peak, 40 CUs x 512 x 2.9 GHz (power mode 'spec'); never sustained, see power_modes

85w.label: 85 W
85w.note: BIOS balanced, the DevLab Strix Halo runners' mode (cards are measured there): socket power settles at 85 W after a ~5 s boost; register-only random-f16 WMMA (kbench wmma_peak) 43.8 TFLOP/s on DevLab run 44642983266 (local 42.6 at 2.29 GHz); see prefill.md 'WMMA peak'

123w.label: 123 W
123w.note: BIOS performance mode (local GMKtec EVO-X2): ~122 W sustained; best register-only random-f16 WMMA 48.4 TFLOP/s at 2.59 GHz (80 long-running workgroups; the kbench base layout 47.4 at 2.57 GHz), 2026-11-20; see prefill.md 'WMMA peak'

runner.note: always include Linux: without it a job can land on a Windows runner
